body:
Between the account and the rival, I side mostly with the rival's ordering and the account's instincts. One thing first: the objection channel here is empty. That does not mean the account passed a test; it means one channel of challenge is silent, and my acceptance of parts of it rests on grounds visible in the material, not on survival.

From the account I keep: the observation that re-litigating the past asks memory to settle something memory cannot settle; the insistence that any remedy be treated as testable rather than adopted; the requirement that any approach to the avoiding friend be curiosity about their experience rather than a plan to retrieve them; and its own commitment, made in passing, that if the approach produces more avoidance, that outcome should count against the framing rather than being read as resistance. From the rival I keep: the underdetermination claim; the probe; the reframing of the one-to-one conversation; and — because the rival itself conceded it 'has not shown that a record makes things worse' — I decline to read its third reading (arguments as standing-negotiation) as a reason to withhold a trial of a record. I keep that reading instead as the interpretive key for what failure would look like.

There is an apparent tension worth dissolving. The account says re-litigating past agreements is the wrong move; the rival proposes asking people about past agreements. These are compatible, because the probe does not ask who was right. It reads the shape of the divergence — scope, recurrence, timing — without adjudicating it, and it uses the most recent case to limit drift. The account's point stands: nobody's memory becomes the verdict. The rival's point stands too: the pattern in the disagreements is still diagnostic.

The plan I would hand back, in order:

First, probe before any system. Ask each flatmate separately, about the most recent disagreement, the rival's question: what did you take us to have agreed to? Two refinements against the interrogation reading the rival itself flagged: ask for each person's own past understanding, not for the true agreement (the rival's phrasing already does this), and offer your own version first, framed as your take rather than the standard.

Second, with the avoiding friend, the probe and the one-to-one approach are one event. Asking for their view of what the group conversations get wrong is simultaneously the rival's reframing and the account's curiosity-first approach — the rival already noticed the probe quietly tests this. If they decline even this, the refusal is data: on the account's own commitment it counts against the reading that they merely need a lower-stakes setting, and the material gives me nothing further to conclude from it.

Third, decide about the record by the shape of what comes back. If the disputes cluster on scope, recurrence, or timing, install the record — but revised. Here is the sharpest thing I can add: the account's own best example of the ambiguity ('every week, by me' versus 'this week, whoever is up') is a recurrence ambiguity, yet its remedy vocabulary — task, person, day, what 'done' means — has no field for recurrence. Each entry therefore needs five fields: task, person, scope (what it covers), recurrence (this once / standing role / rotation), and by-when. Scope and recurrence get said aloud at the moment of agreement; the record is the backstop, not the fix.

Fourth, if the answers do not cluster, do not install a system. I note an internal tension in the rival here: it says non-clustering gives weight to the standing-negotiation reading, and also warns against treating non-clustering as evidence for one's favored reading. I resolve it by treating non-clustering as weak evidence — recollection is noisy — that shifts the next move rather than the verdict: name the pattern to the group ('we keep having this conversation; what is it doing for us?') as a further probe, not as a remedy. Fair warning: that conversation requires all three, and the avoidance is standing evidence it may be the hardest one to convene.

Fifth, sharpen the falsification ladder. The account's own test — arguments persisting after a record plus a definition of 'done' — is better than most, but a system meeting that specification could still fail for the rival's second reading, and the failure would then be wrongly charged to the memory-gap reading alone. A scoped, spoken-at-agreement record that still fails is real evidence against readings one and two and for the third. And if the fight relocates onto the record itself — who writes it, whose tasks appear on it — that is positive evidence for the third reading, not a reason to redesign the record.

The weekly check-in I demote to conditional: attached to a record, its job being to state schedule changes before they bite. A standing meeting without one presumes the three can talk productively, which the avoidance puts in question.

What I reject or demote, with grounds: the account's confidence in the one-to-one approach as the first move — demoted to merged-with-the-probe, on the rival's outnumbered-dynamic worry, which is itself a hypothesis, not an observation. The rival's tacit use of its third reading as a pre-trial veto on the record — rejected, on its own admission of no shown harm. The account's diagnosis as established — rejected as certainty, retained as leading hypothesis.

Left open because the material is silent: whether the household will accept any of this; whether the avoidance is about chores at all, or long-standing rather than recent; whether the load is unequal in some way nobody has named; and what to do if the avoiding friend declines even the low-stakes conversation. On that last one I have no next move, and I would rather mark the boundary than invent one.
commitments:
Taking this up involves the following, offered as proposals rather than settled findings.

Claims I am asking others to accept, each revisable on its own: that the memory-gap reading is the leading hypothesis rather than a diagnosis; that probing precedes installing any system; and that the account's own falsification test (a record plus a definition of 'done') is incomplete because it omits recurrence and spoken scope, so its failure would not discriminate the first two readings. Accepting the underdetermination claim also means accepting that the probe may return nothing decisive, and that non-clustering answers are weak evidence — noisy recollection — which shifts the next move without settling the verdict.

The probe carries a discipline, not just a question: one separate conversation per flatmate, most recent disagreement, each person's own past understanding, my version offered first. Whoever runs it commits to not adjudicating between the answers and not relaying them between flatmates — the moment 'B said X about the dishes' travels, the probe becomes the argument it was meant to diagnose. I inherit the rival's flagged weakness without being able to bound it: recollection is the disputed material, so the probe yields reports about past understandings, not the past, and asking may shape the answers.

The record, if installed, commits to the five fields, recurrence explicitly, with scope and recurrence spoken aloud at the moment of agreement. Consequences accepted: entries cost more than verbal agreements, and the household may read the artifact as overhead or surveillance — a risk the account itself flagged that nothing in the material bounds. Methodologically, anyone running the trial commits to counting failure against readings one and two only after the recurrence/scope version has been tried, and to reading a fight that relocates onto the record as evidence for the standing-negotiation reading rather than as a prompt to redesign. That is a use of the rival's third reading as an interpretation of failure; I rejected its use as a pre-trial veto, on the ground of the rival's own admission that it never showed harm.

On the avoiding friend: merging the account's approach and the rival's probe into one framed event commits me to treating refusal as data that counts against the lower-stakes-setting reading, per the account's own stated commitment — and to not escalating and not reading the refusal as confirmation of anything else. At that point my prescription runs out, and I am committing to marking that boundary rather than filling it with an invented move.

The demotion of the account's one-to-one confidence rests on the rival's outnumbered-dynamic worry, which is a hypothesis about the friend's experience, not an observation of it. The conditional check-in is my own modification: run without a record, it becomes someone else's move, and it presumes all three can talk productively, which the avoidance contests.

Criticisms I am making, with grounds: against the account, that it moved from diagnosis to remedy faster than the material warrants (the rival's ground, accepted); against the rival, that its caution about the record tacitly functioned as a veto while conceding no shown harm. What I am not committing to: the truth of any of the three readings; that the problem is protocol-fixable; that the avoidance is about chores; anything about load distribution, escalation, or the avoidance's history, on which the material is silent. The objection channel being empty means no element of the account has survived a challenge in that channel; acceptance of its surviving parts rests on grounds visible here alone.
